questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

#1681	[enhancement,priority/P3]	feat(datasource): Google BigQuery adapter — the biggest warehouse omission

#685	[enhancement]	feat(connections): purge/redact path for connection version history (immutable snapshots retain edited-out config values)

#2424	[bug,priority/P3]	db: privacy_settings, scoring_settings and llm_settings do not enforce their singleton
#2421	[bug,priority/P3]	docs capture stack: `start` exits before Vite when no LLM server is running

#2240	[security,priority/P2]	security: mask an aggregate min/max metric_value on policy-sensitive columns at read time

#2068	[bug,priority/P3]	bug (latent): RunDetail does not refetch when :runId changes on the same mounted instance

#1824	[bug,priority/P3]	otp: a broker outage on the code-request path burns the caller's per-email quota with no email sent

## Cycle plan — v1.3 (8 weeks, 2026-10-05 → 2026-11-29)

> Confirmed by the maintainer 2026-10-05. **No net-new features this cycle:** build what is
> already on the roadmap or filed, features first (Weeks 1–5), then bug fixes and security
> (Week 6), polish (Week 7), and debt, decisions and the close (Week 8). Every issue open at
> the v1.2 close is in a week below; new filings go to the `v1.3 Backlog` milestone.

### v1.3 Week 1 — coverage & checks (due 2026-10-11)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ✅ | [#1661](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1661) feat(monitors): zero-config auto-baselines — unknown-unknown detection without an authored check — ADR 0047 already covers all but sensitivity config above the check level. Decided 2026-10-13: automatic checks inherit at run time (asset override → workspace setting → built-in default); ADR 0047 amended. Shipped: ADR amendment ([#2422](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2422)), migration `543b75689c8c` ([#2423](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2423)), settings API ([#2425](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2425)), run-time inheritance ([#2426](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2426)), admin and asset UI ([#2427](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2427)), false-positive breakdown by automatic check and by connection. Filed: [#2424](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2424) |
| ✅ | [#2369](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2369) feat(checks): enable/disable a check without deleting it (single and bulk) — migration [PR #2414](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2414), code [PR #2415](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2415) |
| ⬜ | [#1674](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1674) feat(privacy): profiler-side PII auto-detection as an additional classification source — researched 2026-10-07: five design decisions needed before code (see the issue) |
| ⬜ | [#1675](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1675) feat(monitors): pii_drift monitor kind — PII-looking data appearing in an unclassified column — blocked on #1674; also needs a migration widening the kind constraints |
| ✅ | [#1762](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1762) feat(notifications): promote an existing per-suite webhook to a reusable channel — [PR #2412](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2412) (guided in-app action, no migration) |

Filed from this week's reviews, in later weeks: [#2413](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2413) (Week 6), [#2416](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2416) (Week 6), [#2417](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2417) (Week 7).

### v1.3 Week 2 — operating DataQ & the first outside user (due 2026-10-18)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#1704](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1704) ops: backup/restore + tested upgrade path for DataQ's own database (the BYOL survival story) |
| ⬜ | [#1707](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1707) feat(telemetry): opt-in, privacy-respecting product usage telemetry seam (default OFF) |
| ⬜ | [#2387](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2387) Ship THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES (or an SPDX SBOM) in the images and GitHub releases |
| ⬜ | [#2388](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2388) Portable install artifact: a Helm chart (ADR 0013 Phase 2) |
| ⬜ | [#2253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2253) docs(marketing): a walkthrough of the demo profile on the marketing page (video or annotated screenshots) |
| ⬜ | [#1664](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1664) docs(positioning): adopt the 'Data Quality Control Plane' framing on the marketing page + docs site |
| ⬜ | [#2395](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2395) Changelog fragments: one file per PR, assembled at release |
| 🟡 | [#2440](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2440) feat(monitors): per-period metrics with yearly seasonality and seasonal periods on the anomaly monitor — **unplanned, net-new, taken on the maintainer's direction 2026-10-13** in a cycle scoped as no net-new features. ADR 0048 ([#2441](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2441)). Shipped: per-period metrics ([#2442](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2442)), history seeded from the table ([#2444](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2444)), yearly seasonality in scoring for the per-period metrics ([#2445](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2445)). Remaining: declared seasonal calendar, detected periods and their reads, calendar and trend UI, yearly on the whole-table metrics and the automatic-coverage switch. Filed: [#2443](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2443) |

### v1.3 Week 3 — datasources, deploy targets & auth (due 2026-10-25)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#1681](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1681) feat(datasource): Google BigQuery adapter — the biggest warehouse omission |
| ⬜ | [#1683](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1683) feat(datasource): Google Cloud Storage flat-file adapter — completes the object-store trio |
| ⬜ | [#505](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/505) Post-v1: AWS + GCP deploy IaC (behind the provider-agnostic seams) |
| ⬜ | [#2309](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2309) feat(datasources): keyless auth — managed identity / IAM role / workload identity |
| ⬜ | [#2310](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2310) feat(audit): an object-lock tamper anchor (S3 Object Lock / Azure immutable blob) |
| ⬜ | [#717](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/717) Revisit Iceberg v3 support (deletion vectors, row lineage) behind a capability gate — ADR 0030 |

### v1.3 Week 4 — product surfaces (due 2026-11-01)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#1687](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1687) feat(ui): in-app notification center — bell/feed with read-ack + deep links |
| ⬜ | [#1667](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1667) feat(ui): global search / command palette (⌘K) — jump to any suite/check/connection/run by name |
| ⬜ | [#1686](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1686) feat(results): run comparison — diff two runs of a suite |
| ⬜ | [#888](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/888) feat: tagging for suites / assets / connections / checks (workspace labels + list filters) |
| ⬜ | [#1516](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1516) feat(ui): Profile / Workspace-Settings IA pickup — replace the labelled placeholders (deferred-by-design) |
| ⬜ | [#244](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/244) Suite-on-suite triggering (run a suite when another suite completes) |

### v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance (due 2026-11-08)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#1977](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1977) feat: consumer-side data contract validation — contract entity + ODCS import/export |
| ⬜ | [#1689](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1689) feat(integrations): test-management result publishing — TestRail / Xray / Zephyr behind a result-exporter seam |
| ⬜ | [#1690](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1690) feat(catalog): governance-catalog integration — push DQ quality facets + pull classifications (DataHub / OpenMetadata-REST / Collibra seam) |
| ⬜ | [#685](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/685) feat(connections): purge/redact path for connection version history (immutable snapshots retain edited-out config values) |
| ⬜ | [#1613](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1613) RunDetail/RunReport show the check's CURRENT engine/dimension, not as-of-the-result (historical_check_context gap) |
| ⬜ | [#2255](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2255) feat(privacy): a reason per entry in redacted_columns (own tag / inherited tag / policy / value classifier / default mask) |

### v1.3 Week 6 — bug fixes & security (due 2026-11-15)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#2348](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2348) Deleting a check silently rewrites the history of every run it took part in |
| ⬜ | [#2383](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2383) Suggested rules: a value set saved before a column was classified as PII stays readable |
| ⬜ | [#2240](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2240) security: mask an aggregate min/max metric_value on policy-sensitive columns at read time |
| ⬜ | [#2111](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2111) fix(dispatch): send_task from the API subscribes to the Redis result backend per run — extra round-trips and a GC re-entrancy deadlock |
| ⬜ | [#2260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2260) deps: oauthlib 3.3.1 carries CVE-2026-49265/49264 (server-side only); databricks-sql-connector pins oauthlib<4.0.0 |
| ⬜ | [#2374](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2374) checks: a volume check with only min_rows is refused with 'needs integer min_rows/max_rows' although the value given is an integer |
| ⬜ | [#2243](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2243) fix(flatfile): a suite target's file_format is ignored by the run path (profiler-only) |
| ⬜ | [#2133](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2133) Redirect guard: an omitted field and its explicit default compare as 'moved' (Trino auth_type/sslmode) |
| ⬜ | [#2068](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2068) bug (latent): RunDetail does not refetch when :runId changes on the same mounted instance |
| ⬜ | [#1824](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1824) otp: a broker outage on the code-request path burns the caller's per-email quota with no email sent |
| ⬜ | [#1840](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1840) Settings → Notifications tab says a workspace-wide default channel is 'a post-v1 follow-up', but workspace channels exist |
| ⬜ | [#2311](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2311) security(adf): enforce webhook replay/freshness on ADF alerts (firedDateTime) |
| ⬜ | [#2392](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2392) Docs workflow: a release tag's Pages deploy omits the version it just published, and one stuck deploy blocked every publish for four days |
| ⬜ | [#2136](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2136) Flaky test: test_revoke_all_for_user_is_attributed_to_the_actor orders audit events by a tied timestamp |
| ⬜ | [#2413](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2413) Promote to channel: a legacy ref whose secret is gone becomes a channel that never delivers |
| ⬜ | [#2416](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2416) A suite with no runnable check still runs and ends succeeded with zero results (dashboard, gate and coverage read it as clean) |

### v1.3 Week 7 — polish: MCP & API, performance, accessibility (due 2026-11-22)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#2353](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2353) mcp: list_runs returns only the raw triggered_by marker (manual:<user-uuid>), no readable label |
| ⬜ | [#2360](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2360) mcp: list_assets / get_asset do not return the asset health score |
| ⬜ | [#2367](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2367) mcp: get_suite_performance says 'latest completed run' but scores the latest run only if it completed |
| ⬜ | [#1838](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1838) MCP: carry the read-only / state-changing / live-probe classification as ToolAnnotations on each tool; derive GATES and the docs from it |
| ⬜ | [#2356](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2356) llm: SQL generation lists every column of the target in its prompt with no cap |
| ⬜ | [#2354](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2354) alerting: alerts name the provider 'ADF' while the UI and run labels say 'Azure Data Factory' |
| ⬜ | [#1999](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1999) perf(scheduler): dispatch is serial at ~2.4 ms/schedule — 10k due schedules takes 23.6 s of a 60 s beat tick |
| ⬜ | [#2117](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2117) perf(scheduler): the remaining per-schedule dispatch cost is one serial broker publish |
| ⬜ | [#2012](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2012) perf(dashboard): _suite_performance is a DISTINCT ON over the whole runs table — 82 ms at 1M |
| ⬜ | [#2010](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2010) perf(dashboard): the status histogram is still linear at 1M — a materialised per-day rollup is the next step |
| ⬜ | [#1987](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1987) Deep-offset paging on /runs, /pipeline_runs and /incidents is still linear — keyset/seek paging is now viable |
| ⬜ | [#1979](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1979) Partial/expression indexes silently stop applying under server-side parameter binding (psycopg3) |
| ⬜ | [#1597](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1597) audit_chain.verify_chain loads the full hashed audit_events set into memory per call |
| ⬜ | [#2235](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2235) perf(profiler): suggest_policy_for_target on S3/ADLS builds the store client and reads the secret twice |
| ⬜ | [#1672](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1672) a11y(3/4): keyboard traversal + focus management audit |
| ⬜ | [#1673](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1673) a11y(4/4): screen-reader semantics — landmarks, table headers, aria-live run progress, chart text alternatives |
| ⬜ | [#2067](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2067) a11y: detail pages are titled generically — name the suite / asset / check in the document title |
| ⬜ | [#2064](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2064) ux: in-app navigation never resets scroll — a new page opens at the previous page's scroll offset |
| ⬜ | [#2061](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2061) a11y: printing / PDF export from the dark theme inherits dark tokens |
| ⬜ | [#2051](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2051) a11y: the ratchet cannot detect under-reporting — a scan of a half-loaded page passes |
| ⬜ | [#2417](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2417) mcp: incident, history and snooze tools do not say when the check they describe is switched off |

### v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close (due 2026-11-29)

| Status | Task |
|---|---|
| ⬜ | [#2358](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2358) test: test_an_admin_reads_the_log_newest_first fails when backend/tests/services runs before it (audit events leak across tests) |
| ⬜ | [#2135](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2135) test_membership_service is not hermetic: WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS from the repo .env changes its outcome |
| ⬜ | [#2115](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2115) test flake: test_the_access_write_cost_does_not_grow_with_the_result_count fails on CI noise (4.36x > 3.0) on a docs-only PR |
| ⬜ | [#2124](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/2124) ci: run the MySQL / MariaDB live battery against service containers |

=========== #1674
feat(privacy): profiler-side PII auto-detection as an additional classification source
----BODY----
Theme-4 privacy pack, item 1 (context/post-v1-roadmap.md) — the classification remainder left open when #415 closed with #417. The profiler already visits every column: add lightweight format/regex detectors (no LLM) that PERSIST a per-column classification tag, and redaction reads tags instead of name heuristics. Classification sources compose, most-authoritative wins: warehouse tags (#433, shipped) > governance-catalog pull (#1690-class, Theme 14) > profiler heuristics. Note suggest_column_policy already has the heuristics — this issue is about persisting them as a durable source in the ladder, not inventing new detection.
----COMMENTS----
[2026-10-07 TheurgicDuke771]
## Design notes before building (research, 2026-10-07)

Findings that change the shape of this issue and of #1675:

- **The detectors are thinner than the issue assumes.** `column_classification.py` has value detectors for email and encoded blobs (plus uuid/hash for identifiers). There are no phone, SSN, card or IP detectors. "The heuristics already exist" holds for those two only; anything more is new detection.
- **Something is persisted today, once, per suite:** `auto_classify_columns` writes a derived policy into `suites.column_policy` at suite create and never refreshes it. Because `classify_column` defaults an unknown column to PII, that derived `pii_columns` mixes "affirmatively PII" with "unknown".
- **No per-column classification store exists.** The only (asset, column) store is `assets.column_tags`, and profiler verdicts must not go there: it is overwritten on every run from the warehouse, its keys suppress lineage inheritance, its values propagate downstream as warehouse truth, and a `public` value clears a column in fail-closed mode.
- On SQL datasources the profiler's evidence is the 20 most frequent values per column, not a row sample.

## Proposed design

- Two nullable columns on `assets` beside the warehouse-tag pair: `detected_classifications JSONB` (`{column: {verdict, detector, summary}}`, counts only, never values) and its timestamp. Written even when empty, so "looked and found none" differs from "never looked".
- **Additive only.** Persist only `sensitive`. A persisted verdict can add masking and can never clear a column or satisfy fail-closed clearance.
- One new rung, below warehouse tags and the suite policy and above the live name/value heuristic, read through the one choke point every surface already uses (`effective_column_tags`).

## Decisions needed (an ADR, or an amendment to the G3 docs)

1. May a suite's `identifier_column` override a profiler verdict? On Postgres, MySQL, files and Iceberg there is no warehouse tag to clear a false positive, and hash-like IDs can trip the encoded detector.
2. JSONB on `assets` (matches the warehouse-tag precedent) or a normalised `asset_column_classifications` table (suits the future governance-catalog source).
3. Does a re-profile that finds nothing remove an earlier verdict?
4. Detector scope: email and encoded only, or add phone / SSN / card / IP in this issue.
5. Do profiler verdicts propagate along lineage? Recommended: no, only warehouse verdicts do.

#1675 (`pii_drift`) also needs a migration to widen `ck_checks_kind_valid` and `ck_monitor_baselines_kind_valid`; the kind is not reserved in the constraint.

Not started in code.

=========== #2440
feat(monitors): per-period metrics with yearly seasonality and seasonal periods on the anomaly monitor
----BODY----
Requested 2026-10-13. Net-new in a cycle scoped as no net-new features; taken on the maintainer's direction.

## Problem
An anomaly check can only watch whole-table row count, freshness and column profile, and keeps at most eight weeks of history. A table with a yearly rhythm (a sales table with sale periods) raises a false alarm at every recurring peak, and a peak that should have arrived but did not goes unnoticed.

## Decisions taken
- **Metric:** a per-period value bucketed by a date column (rows per day or week, or the sum of a column).
- **History:** hybrid. Seed once from the table's own rows when the check is created, marked as backfilled, then accumulate from every run.
- **Seasonal periods:** both declared by a person and detected from history. They are used to judge the data. A sale-period report for analysts is out of scope: that is business analysis and belongs in a BI tool.
- **Where:** the anomaly monitor as an authored check, not automatic coverage.

## Slices
1. ADR.
2. Per-period metrics: measurement, config validation, observations keyed by period.
3. Seeding from the table, and retention of three years.
4. Yearly seasonality in scoring.
5. Declared seasonal periods (workspace calendar; migration first, in its own PR).
6. Detected periods on the check's trend; MCP and REST reads.
7. Check editor and trend UI; docs.
----COMMENTS----
[2026-10-13 TheurgicDuke771]
## Status, 2026-10-14

Shipped:
- ADR 0048 (#2441).
- Phase 1, per-period metrics `period_row_count` / `period_sum` (#2442).
- Phase 2, history seeded from the table and three-year retention (#2444).
- Phase 3, yearly seasonality in scoring for the per-period metrics (#2445, merging).

Changed during review of phase 3, recorded as amendments in the ADR:
- The yearly score is proportional to the expected value, and earlier years' disagreement about a peak widens the spread.
- Yearly on the whole-table metrics (`row_count`, `freshness_age_hours`) was withdrawn: one stored point a day mis-scored checks that run several times a day. It needs a one-a-day series beside the run-by-run points and is now its own phase, ahead of the automatic-coverage switch.

Remaining:
4. Declared seasonal calendar (migration first, on its own), and attaching entries to a check.
5. Detected periods and the REST/MCP reads.
6. Calendar UI and the trend view drawing the expected value.
7. Whole-table yearly, then the `yearly` switch in the automatic-coverage baseline shape (ADR 0047 amendment).

Also filed from this work: #2443 (a browser-test flake).

content.content:
=========== #1704
ops: backup/restore + tested upgrade path for DataQ's own database (the BYOL survival story)
From the 2026-08-29 gap review (the 'things you never asked for' set, user-accepted). DataQ's own Postgres holds every check, run, result and audit event, and there is: no documented backup/restore runbook for the product (the harness PG was once backed-up→recreated→restored, but that's harness ops, not product docs); no tested VERSION-TO-VERSION upgrade path (migrations are tested individually, never as 'v1.1.0 → v1.2.0 on a populated production DB'); no rollback doctrine for a bad release.

Ship in slices: (1) a docs-site backup/restore + upgrade runbook page (pg_dump/restore, the two-step migration discipline as the user-facing guarantee); (2) a CI job that seeds a previous-release DB and runs `alembic upgrade head` against it — the upgrade-path regression gate; (3) a rollback note per release in the CHANGELOG discipline. The first real customer's first post-demo question is this one.
=========== #2387
Ship THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES (or an SPDX SBOM) in the images and GitHub releases
From the listing readiness checklist (#732), the one distribution obligation the 2026-07-09 licence audit found: preserve upstream copyright/licence notices (MIT/BSD) and Apache-2.0 NOTICE content when distributing images and bundles.

## Scope

- Generate the notices from the installed backend environment and the frontend lockfile (licence text included, not only names).
- Put the file in both images and attach it to each GitHub release.
- Generate in CI/publish so it cannot go stale; fail the build on a strong-copyleft or unknown licence (CONTRIBUTING rule 40, ADR 0031).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Backend and frontend images each contain the notices file.
- [ ] The release workflow attaches it.
- [ ] A dependency under a forbidden licence fails CI.
=========== #2395
Changelog fragments: one file per PR, assembled at release
From the v1.2 retro. Every PR adds its changelog entry at the top of the same list in `docs/site/reference/changelog.md`, so the second of any two open PRs conflicts, a conflicting PR gets no CI, and each needs `main` merged in by hand (a merge commit also skips the pre-commit hooks).

## Scope

- A fragments directory (one small file per PR, named by PR or issue number, with its section: Added / Changed / Fixed / Security / Breaking).
- A script that assembles the fragments into the changelog at release and deletes them; a CI check that a PR touching user-facing code adds a fragment or says it needs none.
- The *Unreleased* section of the published page is built from the fragments, so the docs site still shows unreleased changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Two PRs that each add an entry merge in either order without a conflict.
- [ ] The release checklist names the assemble step.
=========== #1707
feat(telemetry): opt-in, privacy-respecting product usage telemetry seam (default OFF)
From the 2026-08-29 gap review (user-accepted). There is zero signal on how a user actually uses DataQ — pages visited, check types authored, where authoring is abandoned. Build the seam BEFORE the first design partner arrives. Constraints (non-negotiable, state them in the ADR-sized note): default OFF, explicit admin opt-in surfaced in Admin → Settings; event names + counts only — never a table name, column name, SQL string, or credential; self-hostable sink or plain log file first (no third-party analytics dependency — rule 40 + the no-egress posture); the event list is documented and auditable. The deployment-posture page discloses the setting either way.
=========== #2388
Portable install artifact: a Helm chart (ADR 0013 Phase 2)
From the listing readiness checklist (#732). ADR 0013 decided a Helm chart as the customer-deployable artifact. Today the installable paths are the prebuilt-image compose stack (#2220) and the two reference OpenTofu stacks (`deploy/terraform/{azure,aws}`); there is nothing for a customer's own Kubernetes cluster.

## Scope

- Chart for api, worker, beat, frontend and the migrate job (migration gates the roll, as in the deploy workflows).
- Values for the auth mode, the secret-store backend and external Postgres/Redis; no bundled database by default.
- A CI lint + template check, and a kind-based install smoke.

Trigger-gated: pick up when a Kubernetes user asks, or before any marketplace listing that needs it.

content.content:
Exit code 1
## Phases

1. Per-period metrics: measurement, validation, one point per settled period.
2. Seeding from the table and three-year retention.
3. Yearly seasonality in scoring, for the per-period metrics.
4. The declared calendar (schema first, on its own), and attaching entries to a check.
5. Detected periods and the read surfaces (REST, MCP).
6. Check editor, trend view and calendar UI; user docs.
7. Yearly seasonality for the whole-table metrics (a one-a-day series beside the run-by-run
   points), then the `yearly` switch in the automatic-coverage baseline shape, with an
   amendment to ADR 0047.

## Consequences

- A recurring peak stops paging people, and a missing one starts to.
- The first yearly verdict needs a year of history. Seeding supplies it for a per-period
  metric where the table still holds its past. Everywhere else the check waits a year, and
  says so on every result until then.
- One earlier year cannot tell a recurring sale from a one-off. The index uses it anyway,
  because one year is better than none, and the result names how many years stand behind it.
- A backfilled baseline trusts the table's history. Marking the points is what keeps that
  visible.
- Three years of daily points is a larger baseline row than any check has had. It is one JSONB
  value per check and is read once per run. Switching `yearly` on for automatic coverage
  multiplies that by every covered table, which is why it is off by default there.
- Late rows do not revise a judged period. A table that fills in slowly needs a longer
  `settle_hours`, not a re-read.

## Considered and rejected

- **A report of when the sales are**, for analysts to plan from: that is business analysis,
  and a BI tool is the place for it. DataQ shows the periods it detected because they explain
  its verdicts, not as a product of their own.
- **Accumulating only:** no yearly verdict for a year, and two before a period can be called
  recurring, on tables that already hold the history.
- **Backfilling only:** nothing would record what the table held when each run looked, so a
  later restatement would silently rewrite the baseline.
- **Re-reading recent periods on every run** to pick up late rows: it rewrites observed
  points after they were judged, which is the same objection.
- **Yearly seasonality on the per-period metrics alone:** a snapshot table that is replaced
  every night has a row count with seasons too, and the automatic baselines would never get
  it.
- **Comparing only against the same period in earlier years:** two or three points give no
  spread to score against. The index keeps the recent window as the source of spread.
- **Matching by ISO week number:** some years have a week 53 and the earlier year does not.
- **Skipping every verdict inside a declared period with no history:** it would hide a failed
  load during a sale, which is the incident this exists to catch.
- **Letting a detected period change the baseline before a person confirms it:** an
  unreviewed guess would move verdicts with nothing in the result to say so.
- **A calendar entry that applies to every check automatically:** one admin entry would
  change the verdicts of checks on tables the sale never touches.
- **A forecasting library** (seasonal decomposition or similar): a new dependency whose
  verdict cannot be explained from the numbers in the result.
- **Declared periods typed into each check:** the same sale would be entered again for every
  table it touches. A check attaches entries; it does not define them.

   starts empty and waits. Dropping a check's baseline seeds it again.

3. **Yearly seasonality is a seasonal index over the rolling baseline.** With `yearly: true`:

   - The *level* at a period is the median of the `window` periods before it.
   - The *index* for a period is what the matching period in an earlier year was, divided by
     the level then. With more than one earlier year the index is their median.
   - *Matching.* A day is matched to the same weekday nearest the same calendar date in the
     earlier year (52 weeks back, then 104, and so on, corrected to the nearest such
     weekday); a week to the week containing that date. There is no "week 53" case. A peak
     tied to a fixed date (25 December) or to a moving one (a sale) does not line up this
     way, and needs a declared period (decision 4).
   - *Scoring.* The expected value is the level now times the index. The run is scored on
     how far it is from that **in proportion to it**, against how far each prior period was
     from what was expected of it. A sale that ran at 2.4 times its surrounding weeks last
     year is expected at 2.4 times now, so arriving near 2.4 times is normal and arriving
     flat is not; and a sale day five times an ordinary day has five times the room.

     > **Amended 2026-10-14.** As first written the distance was taken in the metric's own
     > units, so a peak had only an ordinary day's room and a sale that repeated within the
     > range of earlier years still alerted. It is proportional now. With two or more
     > earlier years, how much they disagreed about the size of the peak is added to the
     > spread, and the result shows each year's ratio: two years with a sale and one without
     > make a loose comparison, and the check says so instead of pretending to precision.
     > Where the expected value is zero (the shop was closed that day last year) there is no
     > proportion to take, and the distance is taken as it stands.

   - *When it does not apply.* The index is used only where it means something: the level
     then was above zero and neither it nor the matched value is negative. Otherwise, and
     for a period with no earlier year to match, the index is 1, which is exactly today's
     behaviour, and the result says the yearly comparison was not applied and why (no
     earlier year, a zero level, a negative sum).

   Every number in that chain is in the result: the level, the index, the years it came from
   and the expected value. Nothing is skipped for want of a year: the check is useful from
   the day it has `min_points`, and becomes seasonal when the history allows.

4. **Yearly seasonality is a property of the anomaly kind, not of one metric.** It is
   offered on every metric that is one number per run: the two per-period metrics, the
   whole-table row count and the freshness age. For the whole-table metrics a "period" is a
   calendar day, the stored point for a day is the last run's value that day, and history
   can only accumulate: there is nothing to seed a past row count from. Weekday seasonality
   stays as it is and combines with it. The column profile does not get it: it is hundreds
   of series per check, and three years of each is not a baseline, it is a warehouse.

   > **Amended 2026-10-14.** The first build tried "one stored point a day, the day's last
   > run" for the whole-table metrics, and it was wrong: a check that runs hourly was scored
   > against the previous days' last readings (a freshness age of one hour against priors of
   > twenty-one), and switching the setting on or off threw history away. A whole-table
   > metric needs its run-by-run points kept as they are, with a separate one-a-day series
   > for the yearly index beside them. That is its own phase; until it ships, `yearly` is
   > accepted on the per-period metrics only.

   Automatic coverage (ADR 0047) gets it through the setting it already has: the baseline
   shape gains a `yearly` switch, default off, which applies to the automatic row-count and
   freshness baselines. The per-period metrics are **not** added to automatic coverage: an
   automatic baseline assumes nothing about a table, and choosing which column is the
   business date and which is the amount is a claim a person makes. Automatic coverage may
   later *suggest* one for review.

5. **Seasonal periods are declared by people and detected from history. Only declared ones
   change a verdict.**

   - **Declared.** A workspace calendar of named periods, each either recurring (a month and
     day range, every year) or dated (explicit start and end, for a sale that moves). Admins
     manage it; changes are audited. It is workspace-wide because a sale period is a fact
     about the business. A check names the calendar entries that apply to it, and none do by
     default, so adding an entry changes no check until someone attaches it.
   - **What a declared period does.** A day inside it is matched to the same offset within
     that period's previous occurrence, which is what makes a moving sale or a fixed date
     line up. Periods inside it are left out of the level, so the weeks after a sale are not
     judged against the sale. And when the period has no earlier occurrence in the history,
     the check is told a rise is expected and cannot say how large: a value **above** what
     the rolling baseline expects is reported as within the declared period and not banded,
     while a value **below** it is judged as usual. A load that fails during a first-year
     sale still alerts.
   - **Detected.** Read from a check's own history when someone asks: a run of periods at or
     above 1.5 times the level. Seen at the same time in two or more years it is *recurring*;
     in one year, *seen once*. Detected periods are shown on the check's trend so a person
     can see why a verdict came out as it did, and an admin can promote one to the calendar.
     Until then a detected period is a description: it is not stored and it changes no
     score. The seasonal index already carries a recurring peak into the expected value
     without it.

6. **Retention.** A check with `yearly` on, or on a per-period metric, keeps three years of
   periods plus its window (about 1,100 daily points). Other anomaly checks keep what they
   keep today.

## Phases

1. Per-period metrics: measurement, validation, one point per settled period.

content.content:
`backend/tests/conftest.py::_db_engine` runs `Base.metadata.drop_all()` at session teardown on whatever `TEST_DATABASE_URL` points at. Two agents running pytest concurrently against the shared `dataq_test` see ~1000 spurious failures / `UndefinedTable` when the other session tears down mid-run (seen 2026-09-17 on #1986).

**Why:** the schema is per-database, not per-session; the fixture assumes exclusive ownership.

# Changelog

Notable, user-facing changes. Dates are the release/merge date. This is a curated summary —
the per-PR history lives in the repo's commit log and pull requests.

## Unreleased

### Added

- **Anomaly checks on a value per day or week.** Two new anomaly metrics,
  `period_row_count` and `period_sum`, watch the rows or the summed amount in each calendar
  period of a date column, for tables whose whole-table row count only grows. A period is
  judged once it is complete and has settled (`timezone`, `settle_hours`), and each period
  gets one stored point. On its first run a check seeds up to three years of history from
  the table's own rows (marked `backfilled`, apart from what later runs observe), so it
  scores at once; `backfill: false` turns that off.
- **Yearly seasonality for anomaly checks.** With `yearly` on, a per-period anomaly check
  also compares with the same time in earlier years: a peak that came last year is expected
  this year and gets room in proportion to its size, the days after it are not judged
  against it, and a peak that fails to arrive is flagged. It applies once the history
  reaches back a year, which seeding supplies at once, and each result says whether it was
  applied and what was expected.
- **Tune automatic coverage in one place.** The thresholds and history window of the
  automatic row-count, freshness and column-profile checks are now settings, not fixed
  numbers. A workspace admin sets them in **Admin → Settings → Automatic coverage**
  (`PUT /admin/coverage`) and can override them for one table on its asset page
  (`auto_coverage_config` on `PATCH /assets/{id}`); the nearest
  level that sets a group wins, then the built-in default (warn 3, fail 4, critical 6
  deviations; 8 same-weekday runs, 4 before scoring). Sensitivity is set per check, so the
  column profile can be loosened without loosening the others. Automatic checks inherit the
CONTRIBUTING.md:184:39. **Quarterly MCP supply-chain audit:** once a quarter, for each client-side MCP server pinned in `.mcp.json` (see CLAUDE.md Appendix), verify the package hasn't been deprecated, yanked, or transferred to a new publisher (e.g. `npm view <pkg> maintainers time`), and review the changelog before bumping the pinned major version. MCP servers run with local tool access — treat a publisher change like a compromised dependency until verified.

Read /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/641b53ca-47b3-45aa-9ab6-6db8524d561d/scratchpad/AGENT_BRIEF.md first and follow it exactly. Your lane name is `cal` (test DB `dataq_test_cal`).

Task: issue #2440 (milestone "v1.3 Backlog"), ADR 0048 **phase 4 — the declared seasonal calendar**. Read `docs/site/adr/0048-per-period-metrics-yearly-seasonality.md` end to end (decision 5 "Declared", the "Amended 2026-10-14" notes, and "Considered and rejected"), issue #2440 and its status comment (`gh issue view 2440 --comments`), and the shipped code: `backend/app/services/seasonal.py` (History.score), `backend/app/services/anomaly.py`, `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py` (PeriodSpec), the phase 1–3 PRs #2442/#2444/#2445 (`gh pr view N --json body,files`) and their tests under `backend/tests/`. Also read `backend/app/services/coverage_settings_service.py` + its admin route for the pattern of an admin-only, audited settings surface, and `backend/alembic/versions/18f2ee7908cf*` as the migration template; migrations use `autocommit_block()` where needed, and revision ids must not collide with the existing set.

Deliver TWO PRs, in this order, both `Part of #2440` (do not close it):

**PR 1 — migration only** (`chore(db): add seasonal_periods …`): a workspace-wide `seasonal_periods` table — id, name (unique, case-insensitive), kind `recurring|dated`, for recurring a start month/day + end month/day (may wrap the year end), for dated an explicit start/end date, optional note, created/updated timestamps + actor; plus whatever is needed to attach entries to checks. Choose between a join table (`check_seasonal_periods`, FK ondelete RESTRICT so deleting an attached entry is refused and the error names the checks) and a list of ids in the check's JSONB config: pick the join table unless you find a strong reason in the code, and say why in the PR. Backward-compatible, additive only; test `alembic upgrade head` and `downgrade -1` against a real populated Postgres and say so in the PR. Run the `migration-safety` agent on it (spawn it with the Agent tool) and act on what it says.

**PR 2 — service, API and scoring** (`feat(monitors): declared seasonal periods …`):
- Admin-only CRUD for the calendar under `/api/v1/admin/seasonal-periods` (ADR 0033: Admin role; Viewers read-only), audited via the existing `audit_events` mechanism like the other admin mutations (look at how coverage settings / channels are audited and the coverage table test that lists every mutating route — add yours). Validation: recurring ranges valid dates in any year (29 Feb allowed, matched to 28 Feb in a non-leap year — document the rule), dated end >= start, name bounded + NUL-screened like other names.
- Attaching: an anomaly check on `period_row_count` / `period_sum` (and, when phase 7 lands, the whole-table metrics — leave the hook) names entries by id; validated at authoring (`anomaly_params(..., authoring=True)` path) — unknown id refused; a stored check keeps running if an entry vanishes (should not be possible with RESTRICT, but be defensive). Expose the attachments in the check read/export so `check_versions`/export round-trip.
- Scoring in `services/seasonal.py` per ADR decision 5: a day inside a declared period is matched to the same offset within that period's previous occurrence (recurring: previous year's occurrence; dated: the most recent earlier occurrence of the SAME entry name is not a thing — dated entries are one-off, so a dated period matches the previous *recurring-equivalent*? NO: read the ADR literally — a dated entry has no earlier occurrence unless the admin declared one for the earlier year too; treat entries with the same name across years as occurrences of one period only if the schema makes that explicit; if you choose that model, say so in the PR and the ADR amendment). Periods inside a declared period are left out of the *level*. First-year rule: with no earlier occurrence in the history, a value ABOVE the rolling baseline's expectation inside the declared period is reported as `within declared period` and not banded; a value BELOW is judged as usual. Every number used must be in the result payload (which entry matched, offset, matched date, whether first-year applied) — the LLM-facing honesty rule applies: a result must say when a declared period changed the verdict and when it did not.
- Tests: unit tests on the scoring with a NOISY series (an exactly-repeating series hides scale bugs), authz sweep for the admin routes (viewer 403, member 403, admin 200), the audit coverage table, round-trip through export/import and check_versions. Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline.
